article.Citation/Title: Denson, R., & Sydiaha, D. (1970). A controlled study of LSD treatment in alcoholism and neurosis. British Journal of Psychiatry, 116, 443-445.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Denson, R., & Sydiaha, D. (1970) A controlled study of LSD treatment in alcoholism.pdf
article.EligibilityNote: Sample includes alcoholics and neurotics analyzed together; outcomes are the MMPI, Eysenck Personality Inventory, IPAT Anxiety Scale, Lorr Rating Scale, and a general follow-up questionnaire (health, doctor visits, work). No alcohol-consumption, abstinence, craving, or validated SUD-instrument outcome is reported anywhere in the text. Fails criterion (b).
article.InterventionDescription: Oral lysergide (LSD) 50-300mcg (mean 163mcg), preceded by 5mg dextroamphetamine; up to five sessions at 2-week intervals in single hospital rooms; terminated with promazine or chlorpromazine when needed.

article.Outcome: No single primary outcome is designated. The study ran nine comparisons (three timepoint-pairs x Treatment/Control, plus cross-group comparisons at each timepoint) across five instruments (MMPI, Lorr Scale, IPAT, Eysenck/Maudsley Personality Inventory, and a Background/Follow-up Questionnaire) and reports only counts of statistically significant differences per instrument against the number expected by chance at p<.05 (e.g. 'six statistically significant differences... out of a total of 126 comparisons, five per cent of 126 or six... could be expected on the basis of chance'). No instrument or comparison is identified as primary, no SUD-specific outcome is reported anywhere (see EligibilityNote), and the one comparison flagged as 'the only area in which positive results were obtained' (a general-health question) is explicitly deemed 'insufficient to justify rejection of the null hypothesis' by the authors themselves. Selecting any one instrument's count as 'the' effect size would misrepresent a multi-comparison chance-rate analysis as a single primary result, so this is coded '.' per the anti-fabrication rule rather than guessing among five co-equal, non-designated measures.
article.SD: No statistic is paired with a primary Outcome because none was identified (see Outcome rationale). Coded '.'.
article.PVal: No p-value belongs to a single primary comparison; the article reports only significant-vs-chance-expected counts per instrument, not one p-value for one designated outcome. Coded '.'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: No single analysis produces 'the' Outcome, so no single denominator applies. For context: 51 patients were accepted overall (25 Treatment / 26 Control, derived from 'the twenty-five members of the Treatment group' and 51 total); 17 patients per group (34/51) completed 6-month ratings; 13 Treatment and 16 Control (29/51) completed 12-month ratings, with partial data from about half of the remainder. Coded '.'.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 11/14 criteria met. Not described: eligibility (patients were 'referred by Saskatoon psychiatrists for LSD treatment' and 'accepted for the study'; no formal inclusion/exclusion criteria -- diagnostic thresholds, age limits, medical exclusions -- are stated); sample_size_power (no a priori or post hoc power/sample-size discussion anywhere); harms (no Adverse Events/Safety/Side-effects section, table, or explicit statement anywhere -- the promazine/chlorpromazine session-termination detail is procedural intervention description, not a harms assessment). n_met=11 < 13, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 0 (null/negative). The article's own summary states results were 'interpreted as negative' and that 'the supposed therapeutic benefits of LSD treatment in alcoholism and neurosis were not demonstrated by this experiment.' Significant-difference rates across all five instruments approximated the ~5% expected by chance, and the one exception (a general-health question) was explicitly judged insufficient to reject the null hypothesis.
article.Clincial Trial YN: Coded 1, consistent with the eligibility screen: criterion (a) is met (prospectively planned LSD administration, random allocation, defined enrollment of 51 patients over 2 years, an assigned regimen of up to five LSD sessions, and prospective outcome assessment at baseline/6/12 months). Only criterion (b) fails, which does not contradict Clincial Trial YN=1.
article.RandomizationYN: 1. 'Patients... were allocated at random to Treatment and Control groups after undergoing a series of psychological tests.'
article.BlindingYN: 0. 'No attempt was made to use a double or single blind procedure' -- stated explicitly.
article.Double+Blind: 0, consistent with BlindingYN=0 per the field's must-not-contradict rule.
article.Comparator: 1. Waitlist/deferred-treatment control: Control-group patients 'were informed that this type of therapy would be made available to them after a twelve-month waiting period,' while referring psychiatrists continued 'standard treatment' for both groups in the interim.
article.PrimaryCare: 0. Treatment was delivered in a general hospital setting by referring psychiatrists (specialist, not primary-care, providers); no aspect of the study is described as interfacing with primary-care settings or providers.
article.Power: 0. No a priori or post hoc statistical power calculation or discussion appears anywhere; the article discusses only the expected chance rate of significant findings at p<.05 across many comparisons, which is a multiplicity/chance argument, not a power discussion.
article.Retention (%): 56.9 = 29/51 x 100, using the randomized N (51; enrolled and randomized are the same cohort here) as denominator and the longest-follow-up (12-month) completers as the numerator: 13 Treatment + 16 Control = 29 of 51 patients completed 12-month ratings ('this had fallen to 13 in the Treatment group and 16 from the Controls'). Not calculated from the 6-month figure (17+17=34/51=66.7%) because Followup in months (12) reflects the longest reported horizon. Not within 2 points of 80, so no additional near-threshold flag applies.
article.ConfoundYN: 1. The article substantively discusses a confound: baseline (time-1) differences between Treatment and Control on the Questionnaire data (Control patients more frequently reported seeing their doctor about physical complaints and that their feelings interfered with work), explicitly interpreted as evidence 'that the matching of Treatment and Control samples was not perfect,' though judged to have 'no bearing on the effects of treatment.'
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: 0. No explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria are stated beyond psychiatrist referral 'for LSD treatment' and subsequent 'acceptance' into the study; no diagnostic thresholds, age limits, or medical/psychiatric exclusions are given.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: 1. The test battery comprised the Eysenck Personality Inventory, the IPAT Objective Anxiety Scale, the MMPI, and the Lorr Multidimensional Rating Scale (Out-patient Form) -- all validated psychometric instruments.
article.Funding/COI YN: 1. 'This project was supported by National Health Research Grant 607-7-68.' No separate conflict-of-interest statement appears, but funding source disclosure alone satisfies this field.
article.BaseStatus: Coded '.': no severity descriptor (Mild/Moderate/Severe) or severity-mapping language for the alcoholism/neurosis diagnoses is given anywhere; only diagnostic category counts, which sit in the scrambled Table I and are not usable (see PercentFem).
article.Age_Median: Bracket '30-50': 'The age range extended from 17 to 54 years with a median of 33 and a mean of 33.'
article.PercentFem: Coded '.'. Table I (classification of subjects by group, sex and diagnosis) was flattened by the text conversion into an unattributable column of loose digits and dot-leaders near the top of the file (per the fidelity note flagging a garbled table). No digit in that column can be confidently mapped to a Male/Female/Total cell for either group, so per the anti-fabrication instruction this was left uncoded rather than reconstructed with a guessed decoding rule.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Coded '.': race/ethnicity of the sample is never reported anywhere in the article.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: 0. No income, occupational, insurance, or other SES information is reported for the sample anywhere in the text.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: NonUS. The study was conducted in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada (patients referred by 'Saskatoon psychiatrists,' data analyzed at the 'Computer Centre of the Saskatoon Campus, University of Saskatchewan'; author affiliations list the 'Saskatchewan Department of Public Health' and 'University of Saskatchewan, Saskatoon').
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: 0. The sample was psychiatrist-referred specifically 'for LSD treatment' rather than drawn from a general or consecutive clinical population, and the article gives no indication of broader community/clinical representativeness; this constitutes a selected referral sample rather than a real-world representative one. Judgment call given limited detail.
article.InterventionDescription: Summarized from the Treatment section: oral lysergide 50-300mcg (modal 100mcg, mean 163mcg) preceded by 5mg dextroamphetamine to reduce induction-phase anxiety; up to five sessions at two-week intervals in single hospital rooms; state terminated with promazine or chlorpromazine when necessary.
article.InterventionTherapy: 0. No preparation, integration, or psychotherapy component tied to the LSD sessions themselves is described; assessments during sessions were performed by uninvolved staff. 'Standard treatment' continuing via referring psychiatrists is described as ongoing usual care applied identically to both Treatment and Control groups, not as a therapy component added to the LSD intervention.
article.HarmsAssessed: 0, consistent with SafetyReported='N'. No Adverse Events/Safety/Side-effects section, table, or explicit statement exists. The detail that the psychedelic state 'was terminated by an injection of promazine or chlorpromazine when necessary' is procedural intervention-delivery description (ending a session so a patient could be assessed fit to leave), not a reported assessment of harms or adverse events across the sample -- there is no count, no description of what necessitated termination, and no statement characterizing it as an adverse reaction. This is a genuine judgment call, flagged here per the instruction to avoid understating harm; it was resolved toward SafetyReported='N' because no explicit AE/safety framing accompanies the detail anywhere in the article.
article.Followup in months: 12. Testing was planned 'at six months and at twelve months'; twelve months is the longest reported follow-up horizon, measured from treatment (baseline testing occurred 'before allocation to the groups').
article.BehaviorChangeMeasured: 0. No use-frequency, craving, or compulsive-behavior measure is reported for either group; the five instruments used (MMPI, Eysenck, IPAT, Lorr, general questionnaire) are personality/psychiatric-symptom measures, not substance-use-behavior measures. Consistent with the eligibility failure on criterion (b).
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: 0. No biomarker, physiological measure, or vital-sign outcome is reported as a study outcome (the LSD/dextroamphetamine/promazine dosing details are intervention description, not outcome measurement).
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: 1. The MMPI, Eysenck Personality Inventory, IPAT Objective Anxiety Scale, and Lorr Multidimensional Rating Scale are all psychiatric-symptom/personality outcome measures.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: 0. No dedicated quality-of-life instrument is used; the general-health question within the follow-up questionnaire is a single item, not a QoL instrument.
article.Implementation Outcome: 0. No feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, reach, adoption, or sustainability outcome is discussed anywhere.
article.ReductionMeasured: 0. No partial-reduction-in-use outcome is reported anywhere in the text.
article.CessationMeasured: 0. No abstinence/cessation outcome is reported anywhere in the text.
article.RelapseMeasured: 0. No relapse or return-to-use tracking is reported anywhere in the text.
article.MortalityMeasured: 0. Mortality is never addressed as an outcome or otherwise anywhere in the article.
article.LSD: 1. Lysergide (LSD) is the sole study intervention administered to the Treatment group.
article.OtherPsychedelic: 0. Dextroamphetamine (anxiolytic premedication) and promazine/chlorpromazine (used to terminate the drug state) are adjunct pharmacological agents around the LSD sessions, not separate psychedelic interventions, so neither sets OtherPsychedelic.
article.SafetyReported: N. No Adverse Events, Safety, or Side-effects section, table, or explicit statement exists anywhere in the article. See HarmsAssessed rationale for discussion of the borderline promazine/chlorpromazine termination detail, which was judged to be intervention-delivery description rather than a safety report.
article.AE_denominator: '.' (never 'NA' per convention) because no safety assessment was reported.
article.ArmScope: NA because SafetyReported='N'; no AE values exist to scope to an arm.
article.EligibleYN: N. Criterion (a) is met (a genuine randomized controlled trial with defined enrollment, assigned regimen, and prospective outcome assessment). Criterion (b) fails: the five outcome instruments (MMPI, Eysenck, IPAT, Lorr, general follow-up questionnaire) are personality/psychiatric-symptom measures; no consumption, abstinence, cessation, relapse, craving, withdrawal, dependence-severity, or validated-SUD-instrument outcome is reported anywhere in the text, despite the sample including alcoholics.

config_proposal.note: No single primary outcome or effect size is designated among the battery of measures (MMPI, Lorr, IPAT, Eysenck/Maudsley, general questionnaire); the article reports only counts of statistically significant comparisons approximating the ~5% rate expected by chance for each instrument, rather than one primary comparison's statistic, and explicitly concludes the therapeutic benefit was 'not demonstrated.' No defensible single conversion exists, and the study reports no SUD-specific outcome at all.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Significant-difference counts across MMPI (6/126), Lorr (2/90), IPAT (0), Eysenck/Maudsley (2/27), and Questionnaire (9/165) comparisons approximate the ~5% rate expected by chance; the one nominally 'positive' finding (general health) is explicitly deemed insufficient by the authors, who conclude the results were negative/null overall.
